title: Deployment Validation Dojo — Facilitator Notes and Slide Outline
body:
Summary:
This doc is the facilitator playbook for a customer-facing half-day workshop we call the 'Deployment Validation Dojo'. The goal is to run a focused, technical POC loop with customer engineers and platform owners to validate: performance (latency/throughput), functional fidelity vs. baseline prompts, and operational controls (rollbacks, routing, KV cache priming). This session is designed to complement the formal POC run: short, interactive, engineering-first, with clear next-step artifacts.
agenda:
Timebox (3.5 hours total)
- 0:00–0:10 (10m) — Welcome + Objectives (host: Priya)
  - Quick intros (name, role, primary POC goal)
  - State success criteria for today
- 0:10–0:30 (20m) — Architecture & Baseline (host: Marcus)
  - Customer infra diagram walk-through (customer)
  - Redwood serving variants we'll exercise: hosted vs. dedicated vs. local-private shim
- 0:30–1:00 (30m) — Warm-up: Prompt Sensitivity Quicktest (host: Ethan)
  - Run 3 short prompts across model variants; log token usage + outputs
  - Observe regressions; collect 2 example failures for later repro
- 1:00–1:20 (20m) — Latency Ladder & Throughput Planning (host: Lina)
  - Mini exercise: map expected qps and SLOs to instance sizing
  - Identify peak windows + acceptable degradation percent
- 1:20–1:40 (20m) — Breakout #1: Smoke Tests & Canary Plan (two groups)
  - Group A: Define smoke test checklist (functional + perf thresholds)
  - Group B: Draft canary rollout steps and automatic fallback triggers
- 1:40–2:00 (20m) — Lunch stretch / informal demos (optional)
- 2:00–2:30 (30m) — Live Run: KV Cache Priming + Batching Effects (host: Marcus)
  - Demonstrate cache warm vs cold for representative session
  - Run controlled batch sizes and observe p50/p95/p99 token latencies
- 2:30–3:00 (30m) — Resilience Simulation: Capacity Failure & Fallbacks (host: Priya)
  - Simulate a dedicated pool outage; validate routing fallback to hosted variant
  - Exercise automatic rollback on quality regressions
- 3:00–3:25 (25m) — Breakout #2: Runbook & Owner Map
  - Each breakout drafts the operational runbook for oncall and SRE handoff
  - Define activation steps, eskalation path, and rollback owner
- 3:25–3:30 (5m) — Wrap-up, actions, and immediate next steps
  - Assign owners and time windows for post-workshop POC sprints
slide_outline:
Slide deck skeleton (approx 12–16 slides):
1) Title & Goals (1 slide) — Workshop name, date, attendees, 3 measurable objectives
2) POC Boundary & Success Metrics (1 slide) — Functional correctness targets, latency SLOs, cost/throughput targets
3) Customer Infra Snapshot (1 slide) — simple diagram (who owns network, where KMS sits, VPC egress)
4) Redwood Serving Variants Overview (1 slide) — differences and expected tradeoffs
5) Baseline Results (1–2 slides) — quick table: baseline (customer) vs. hosted vs. dedicated p50/p95 and token cost
6) Prompt Sensitivity Findings (1 slide) — 3 prompt examples and short diffs
7) Latency Ladder & Sizing Heuristics (1 slide) — sample qps->GPU mapping
8) KV Cache Primer (1 slide) — why priming matters + how we measure
9) Canary & Smoke Test Blueprint (1 slide) — checklist and automated signals
10) Resilience & Fallback Matrix (1 slide) — routing policies and fallbacks with owners
11) Operational Runbook Template (2 slides) — runbook skeleton + escalation flowchart (text bullets)
12) Breakout Prompts & Deliverables (1 slide) — what each group should produce in 20–25 minutes
13) Open Questions & Assumptions (1 slide) — callouts for product/security/legal follow-up
14) Post-Workshop Commitments & Next Steps (1 slide) — owners, dates, success gates
Notes for speakers: keep slides visual. Avoid long paragraphs; include exact commands and example curl snippets in appendix slides.
facilitation_notes:
Prework for customer (send 72h before):
- Minimal reproducible dataset (sample 50–200 items) with labels where applicable
- A small infra diagram and service account with read-only access to metrics (or screenshots exported)
- API keys / routing rules to test (redacted production keys ok if scoped)
- One representative prompt set saved as JSON\Room setup and logistics:
- Recommended: shared Slack channel or ephemeral Google Meet chat for live logs
- Have terminal access for two seats from each side (customer + Redwood)
- Runbook template printed and editable (digital copy in drive)\Running the sessions:
- Timeboxing is critical — call out the time remaining at 10/5 minute marks
- Encourage everyone to verbalize assumptions before testing
- Use the breakout groups to offload operational detail writing; facilitators should rotate between groups to capture artifacts
- Capture immediate failures as JIRA issues with reproduction steps (owner: recording scribe)\Critical measurement checklist (what to capture during test runs):
- p50/p95/p99 token latencies per-model-variant
- tokens-per-request and tokens-per-second observed
- model output diffs (short examples with expectation vs actual)
- cost estimate delta (rough per-token cost * qps projection)
- error rates and types (timeouts, OOM, truncated responses)\Failure modes to demonstrate and remediation scripts:
- Cold KV cache -> slow initial responses: mitigation = cache-priming job + client-side warmups
- Burst qps causing queue growth -> mitigation = autoscaler tuning + queue-size guardrail
- Model-quality regression after quantization -> mitigation = rollback policy + human-in-the-loop blocking gate
- Network egress blocking VPC -> mitigation = routed proxy + partial fallback to hosted variant (scrub sensitive data)\Ownership and follow-ups:
- Within 48 hours: consolidated test logs + runbook draft (owner: Priya)
- Within 5 business days: scope of Dedicated sizing proposal and cost estimate (owner: Lina)
- Within 10 business days: production canary plan with automated observability checks (owner: Customer Eng lead)\Templates and reproducible snippets (appendix):
- Example curl smoke test for text generation: curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <KEY>" -d '{"model":"rwd-1-small","prompt":"<PROMPT>","max_tokens":128}' | jq .
- Simple latency measurement (bash): for i in {1..100}; do t0=$(date +%s%3N); curl -s -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/generate" -H "Authorization: Bearer <KEY>" -d '"{"model":"rwd-1-small","prompt":"ping","max_tokens":1}"' >/dev/null; t1=$(date +%s%3N); echo $((t1-t0)); done | awk '{sum+=$1; if($1>p95) p95=$1} END{print "avg:",sum/NR,"ms"}'
- Postmortem quick template: short desc, timeline, root cause conjecture, immediate mitigation, long-term fix, owner, ETA\Session artifacts to upload to Drive after: lab-run-logs.zip, smoke-test-results.csv, runbook-first-draft.md, breakout-deliverables.pdf\Open questions to resolve in follow-ups (capture on slide "Open Questions & Assumptions"):
- Data retention and encryption requirements for cache-priming flows
- Whether customer legal needs dedicated audit trail for hosted failover runs
- Acceptable cost delta for temporary hosted fallback (max percent increase)\Facilitator heuristics: when to stop a live test and pivot to discussion: any test causing >3x expected latency increases or unexpected quality regressions. Use that as a signal to escalate rather than continue noisy experiments.\End of facilitator notes.
